answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can use a public work-history graph: every completed job is signed by both parties, so reputation equals real, counterparty-attested work. A new identity starts with an empty meadow of history - no track record, no credit - and counterparties cap exposure to strangers. Forging a convincing history means actually doing the work, paying compute and time per entry, while the delta between one genuine record and a thousand fabricated ones is the cost an attacker must bear. A fable of instant trust collapses: trust is earned transaction by transaction, not claimed.
